key_insight: The paper maps where passive flow control around a rotating cylinder will help or hurt drag, lift, and torque using adjoint sensitivity fields, showing spinning ratio is the main driver of the topology.
engineering_relevance: These sensitivity atlases give practical design guidance for passive devices near Flettner rotors and other rotating cylinders to improve aerodynamic performance over a broad operating range.
method: Topological adjoint sensitivity analysis with a porous-medium formulation
Computed local sensitivity fields for drag, lift, and torque across Re = 1e1 to 1e7 and spinning ratio 0 to 2π
Validated with forward simulations using distributed Darcy-type source terms and a sensitivity-informed passive control structure
evidence_signal: The abstract reports validation by dedicated forward simulations and a systematic sweep over Reynolds number and spinning ratio to build and assess the sensitivity atlas.
watch_item: The atlas is most robust over moderate operating ranges, so designs may need re-checking outside the validated envelope or when geometry/manufacturing details change.
paper_title: Adjoint Sensitivity Maps for Passive Flow Control Around Rotating Circular Cylinders Across a Wide Operating Envelope
